classes.name: Oral corticosteroids
classes.description: Systemic oral corticosteroids: prednisone (tablets, solution; Rayos delayed-release appears discontinued), methylprednisolone (Medrol, dose pack), prednisolone (solution, Orapred ODT, Millipred), dexamethasone (tablets, solution, Dexamethasone Intensol, TaperDex/Dxevo/HiDex packs; Hemady 20 mg is labeled for multiple myeloma only, an alternative, never the pick), hydrocortisone (Cortef; Alkindi Sprinkle and Khindivi oral solution for children). Deflazacort (Emflaza) and vamorolone (Agamree) for Duchenne are specialty alternatives only, never the pick. Not budesonide (Entocort, Uceris, Tarpeyo) or inhaled/topical steroids.
classes.plainDescription: Short courses of steroid pills that calm inflammation fast, for flares of asthma, COPD, arthritis, allergies and more.
classes.indication: Inflammatory flares, asthma/COPD exacerbations, autoimmune disease, adrenal insufficiency

preferredAgent.sig: Dose by condition, 5 to 60 mg by mouth daily, with food (label). A common short course for a flare is 40 mg once daily for 5 days (practice, not label text); taper courses longer than 2 to 3 weeks.
preferredAgent.sigShort: 5-60 mg QD; flare often 40 mg x5d
preferredAgent.plainSig: Take with food in the morning, at the dose and for the days your prescriber sets.

records.verificationNote: Read CDL p.173-176 (glucocorticoids) and p.210-214 (ophthalmic/nasal steroid sections, not picks). Prednisone tablets 1-50 mg carry no UM code; prednisone 10 mg is the pick (judgment). Methylprednisolone, prednisolone and hydrocortisone tablets carry no UM code. Brand names (Medrol, Orapred ODT, Millipred, Cortef, Dxevo/TaperDex packs) are not printed; generic names cover them. The brief's note on Hemady: its 20 mg strength is absent and the only dexamethasone tablets are 0.5-6 mg. [Sonnet check 2026-11-18: Prednisone is tablets only (p.176), dexamethasone tablets 0.5-6 mg (p.174), no deflazacort, no dexlansoprazole-type exceptions; Rayos, Hemady and Emflaza stay pa under CDL p.4.]

records.verificationNote: Prednisone tablets are Tier 1, no flag (PDF p.79). Medrol and Orapred brands are not printed, but generic methylprednisolone and prednisolone solution are covered. Brand-only and specialty products named in the class description are absent and recorded nonformulary (PDF p.6). Orapred ODT is an absent dosage form of a listed drug, not a brand-only product, so it is not recorded (formulary dosage-form caveat, PDF p.10). Injectable Solu-Medrol and Solu-Cortef (p.79) are not used. No PA or step therapy (PDF p.6-7). [Sonnet check 2026-11-18: removed 7 brand-only item(s) inferred nonformulary from absence; p.2 says the formulary 'is not an all-inclusive list' and the p.6 line is only the template definition of 'formulary', so absence is not a nonformulary finding; Kaiser prints no PA/ST (p.6-7)]
